get.description:
Fetch a single product-to-product link: the record connecting `product_id` to `related_product_id` under `relationship_id`.

> **Warning:** This endpoint returns `404 NotFoundError` for links that do exist, the same underlying problem that makes its [collection form](/docs/reference/v3/relatedproducts/get_related_products_collection_api_v3_products__product_id__relationships__relationship_id__related_products_get) come back empty. Don't use it to check whether two products are linked. Use [Search-Related-Products](/docs/reference/v3/relatedproducts/search_related_products_api_v3_related_products_get) with `?product_id=<id>` instead.

All three path segments take Plytix IDs, not SKUs.

Fetch a single field from one product-to-product link, such as `quantity`, instead of the whole record.

> **Warning:** This resolves the link through the same lookup as [Get-Related-Products Identity](/docs/reference/v3/relatedproducts/get_related_products_identity_api_v3_products__product_id__relationships__relationship_id__related_products__related_product_id__get), which can't find links that do exist, so expect the same `404` here. Read a link's fields through [Search-Related-Products](/docs/reference/v3/relatedproducts/search_related_products_api_v3_related_products_get) with `?product_id=<id>` and `_fields` instead.

All path segments take Plytix IDs, not SKUs.

List the products linked to one product under a single relationship type.

> **Warning:** This endpoint returns an empty `data` array even when the relationship has live links. Use [Search-Related-Products](/docs/reference/v3/relatedproducts/search_related_products_api_v3_related_products_get) with `?product_id=<id>` instead.

Both path segments take Plytix IDs: `product_id` is the product's `id`, not its SKU, and `relationship_id` is the ID of the relationship type, from [Search-Relationships](/docs/reference/v3/relationships/search_relationships_api_v3_relationships_get). To see which relationship types a product takes part in, use [Get-Product-Relationships Collection](/docs/reference/v3/productrelationships/get_product_relationships_collection_api_v3_products__product_id__relationships_get).

Fetch a single family-attribute link by its two IDs. Returns the one record: `{product_family_id, attribute_id, level, account_id}`.

Use this to check whether a specific attribute applies to a family. If it isn’t linked, the response is `404` with a `NotFoundError` describing the missing association.

To list every attribute on the family instead, use [Get-Family-Attributes Collection](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/get_family_attributes_collection_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes_get).

post.description:
Link an attribute to a product family, taking `attribute_id` from the URL instead of the request body. It needs no body, and is otherwise the same action as [Post-Family-Attributes Collection](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/post_family_attributes_collection_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes_post).

If the attribute is already linked to that family, this returns `409 AlreadyExists` rather than linking it twice.

Use the collection form when you want to set the attribute’s `level` in the same call; this form always links at the family’s default.

delete.description:
Unlink an attribute from a product family. Returns `204` with no body, after which a `GET` on the same pair returns `404`.

This removes only the link, the attribute itself stays in your account and stays available to other families. To delete the attribute everywhere, use [Delete-Product-Attributes](/docs/reference/v3/productattributes/delete_product_attributes_api_v3_product_attributes__identifier__delete).

> **Warning:** The link is what makes an attribute apply to products in the family, so unlinking changes every product in it, not one. Attribute membership is excluded from [Update-Product-Families](/docs/reference/v3/productfamilies/update_product_families_api_v3_product_families__identifier__patch) for the same reason. Check the family’s `total_products` before unlinking.

patch.description:
Change an existing family-attribute link’s `level`, moving the attribute between the family’s inheritance tiers: `no_level`, `parent_level`, or `variant_level`. Raising an attribute to `parent_level` is what makes a parent’s values flow down to its variants.

> **Warning:** This requires the automatic-inheritance feature on your account. Without it, every level change returns `403 PermissionError` with "Automatic inheritance is not available for this account", whatever the target level. That’s an account-plan gate rather than a problem with the request; contact your account manager to have the feature enabled.

`level` is the only part of a link that can be updated. To change which attributes a family has, link and unlink them with [Post-Family-Attributes Collection](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/post_family_attributes_collection_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes_post) and [Delete-Family-Attributes Identity](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/delete_family_attributes_identity_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes__attribute_id__delete).

get.description:
Fetch a single field from one family-attribute link, such as `level`, instead of the whole record.

A link holds only `product_family_id`, `attribute_id`, `level`, and `account_id`, so there’s rarely a reason to use this over [Get-Family-Attributes Identity](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/get_family_attributes_identity_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes__attribute_id__get), which returns all four in one call.

delete.description:
Delete a single field from a family-attribute link.

> **Warning:** Don’t use this to clear a `level`. Subpath deletes elsewhere in the v3 API don’t perform scoped field removal, and act on the parent record instead of the single field named in the path. To take an attribute off a family, use [Delete-Family-Attributes Identity](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/delete_family_attributes_identity_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes__attribute_id__delete); to move it between tiers, use [Patch-Family-Attributes Identity](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/patch_family_attributes_identity_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes__attribute_id__patch).

patch.description:
Update a single field on a family-attribute link. `level` is the only field a link exposes for update, so this does the same job as [Patch-Family-Attributes Identity](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/patch_family_attributes_identity_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes__attribute_id__patch), with the field name in the path rather than the body.

> **Warning:** The same account-plan gate applies. Without the automatic-inheritance feature, a level change returns `403 PermissionError` with "Automatic inheritance is not available for this account".

Prefer the identity endpoint, which takes the change as an ordinary partial update.

get.description:
List every attribute currently linked to one product family. This is the per-family view of the same link records returned by [Search-Family-Attributes](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/search_family_attributes_api_v3_family_attributes_get), scoped by the `product_family_id` in the path, so it needs no account filter.

Each record is `{product_family_id, attribute_id, level, account_id}`. `level` is the attribute’s inheritance tier within the family: `no_level`, `parent_level`, or `variant_level`.

The response carries attribute IDs, not full attribute definitions. Resolve names and types with [Search-Product-Attributes](/docs/reference/v3/productattributes/search_product_attributes_api_v3_product_attributes_get).

Responses come back in a single page with no `next_page` link, so don’t build paging logic around this endpoint.

`product_family_id` is the family’s Plytix `id`, from [Search-Product-Families](/docs/reference/v3/productfamilies/search_product_families_api_v3_product_families_get), not its name.

post.description:
Link an existing attribute to a product family, so that products in the family can carry that attribute.

Send `{"attribute_id": "<id>"}`. The attribute has to exist already. Create it first with [Create-Product-Attributes](/docs/reference/v3/productattributes/create_product_attributes_api_v3_product_attributes_post). A successful call returns `201`.

`level` is optional and sets the attribute’s inheritance tier in this family (`no_level`, `parent_level`, or `variant_level`). Omit it and the attribute is linked at `no_level`.

> **Warning:** `parent_level` and `variant_level` require the automatic-inheritance feature on your account. Without it, setting either returns `403 PermissionError` with "Automatic inheritance is not available for this account", and only `no_level` links can be created. See [Patch-Family-Attributes Identity](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/patch_family_attributes_identity_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes__attribute_id__patch) for the same gate on changing a level later.

To link by URL instead of in the body, use [Post-Family-Attributes Identity](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/post_family_attributes_identity_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes__attribute_id__post). Use this collection form when you want to set `level` in the same call.

get.description:
Search and list the products in your catalog. With no filters, this returns every product in the account.

Narrow the results with query-string filters, for example `sku=BAG-10157` or `categories.name=Backpacks`. See [Filtering and query syntax reference](/docs/reference/v3/filtering-query-syntax) for the full set of operators.

Use `_fields` (repeatable) to select only the fields you need. Requesting a relationship field such as `categories` or `assets` returns it fully expanded, with no extra call and no `_expand` parameter needed.

Results are paginated at 25 products per page by default. Set `_page_size` to change that, and follow the `next_page` link in the response's `pagination` object to get the next page instead of building your own offset logic.

post.description:
Create a single product.

The response returns the full created product, including its generated `id`, not the ID on its own.

To create a variant, include `parent_id` and `product_family_id` so the new product joins an existing product family hierarchy. See [Reconstruct parent/variant hierarchies](/docs/guides/reconstructing-parent-variant-hierarchies).

If the `sku` you send already exists in the account, this returns `409 Conflict` instead of creating a duplicate.

Add a field to a product. Use the product's Plytix `id` as `identifier`, not its SKU.

To set an attribute value, use [Update-Products](/docs/reference/v3/products/update_products_api_v3_products__identifier__patch) with `{"attributes": {"<name>": "<value>"}}`.

get.description:
Fetch a single field from a product without pulling back the entire product record.

Use the product's Plytix `id` as `identifier`, not its SKU.

> **Warning:** The `categories`, `assets`, and `static_lists` subpaths return an empty array even when the product genuinely has those links. Don't use them to check membership, and don't treat an empty result as proof that a write didn't apply. Read those fields through the search endpoint instead, with `_fields`, for example `GET /products?sku=BAG-10157&_fields=categories&_fields=assets`. The `relationships` subpath is unaffected and returns real data.

patch.description:
Update a single field on a product without sending the whole record.

The `path` is the field name, and the request body is that field's new value on its own, not an object wrapping it. That's a different shape from [Update-Products](/docs/reference/v3/products/update_products_api_v3_products__identifier__patch), which takes a partial product object. Use the root PATCH to change several fields at once, and this one to change exactly one.

Use the product's Plytix `id` as `identifier`, not its SKU.

Plytix checks `path` against the fields a product accepts on an update, so a name it doesn't recognize returns `422` instead of creating anything. A successful call returns `200` with the full updated product.

delete.description:
Delete a single field from a product. In practice this does not provide scoped removal of a link.

A recognized collection name, such as `DELETE /products/{id}/categories`, returns `405 Method Not Allowed` because there's no single well-defined write target. Any other path, including the three-segment `/categories/{category_id}` unlink form, returns `404 Not Found`. The product is left intact in both cases.

To remove one category, asset, or relationship, PATCH the product with the reduced array instead. See [Safely remove categories, assets, or relationships](/docs/guides/safely-removing-categories-assets-or-relationships).

get.description:
Fetch a single product by its Plytix product `id`. This always returns the full product record. It doesn't support `_fields` filtering the way [Search-Products](/docs/reference/v3/products/search_products) does.

The `identifier` must be the product's Plytix ID, not its SKU, even though SKU is the natural key for most catalogs. If you only have a SKU, look it up first with [Search-Products](/docs/reference/v3/products/search_products) (filter on `sku=<value>` with `_fields=id`), then use the returned `id` here.

patch.description:
Update selected fields on a product. Send only the fields you want to change; any field you omit is left untouched.

The response returns the full updated product, not only the fields you sent. It's the same shape a GET on the product returns, including the `assets`, `categories`, and `relationships` arrays.

Use the product's Plytix `id` as `identifier`, not its SKU.

PATCH with a reduced array is the only confirmed way to remove a single category, asset, or relationship link, because the delete-by-subpath endpoint doesn't perform scoped removal. See [Safely remove categories, assets, or relationships](/docs/guides/safely-removing-categories-assets-or-relationships).

Two constraints to know:

- Sending `parent_id` and `product_family_id` together returns `422`. A variant inherits family membership from its parent, so omit `product_family_id` when you set `parent_id`.
- `channel_ids`, `ecatalog_ids`, and `product_data_sheet_ids` require the UEF feature on your account. Without it, including any one of them fails the whole request with `403`, and none of the other fields in that request are applied.

delete.description:
Permanently delete a single product by its Plytix product `id`. This can't be undone: once deleted, the product's data and its links to categories, assets, and relationships are gone.

Use the product's Plytix ID here, not its SKU. If you only have a SKU, look it up first with [Search-Products](/docs/reference/v3/products/search_products).

get.description:
Search the individual product-to-product links in your catalog. Each record is one pair (`product_id`, `related_product_id`, `quantity`, and `last_modified`) which makes this the dependable way to find out which products sit on the other end of a product's relationships.

> **Warning:** Always send a filter. This endpoint is not automatically scoped to your own account the way the rest of the v3 API is, so a call with no filter returns a result set that isn't limited to your catalog. Filter by `product_id` to list one product's related products, or by `account_id` to scope the search to your account.

A product's own `product_relationships` field lists each link's `quantity` and `last_modified` but not its `related_product_id`, so that field alone can't tell you which product a link points to. This endpoint can.

Filtering by `relationship_id` isn't supported: it isn't a field on this resource, and sending it returns `500` with a `HiddenFieldError` rather than the usual `400`. When the relationship type matters, use [Search-Product-Relationships](/docs/reference/v3/productrelationships/search_product_relationships_api_v3_product_relationships_get) instead, which groups links by `relationship_id`.

`_fields`, `_page`/`_page_size`, and `_sort_by` work as they do on the other search endpoints. See [Filtering and query syntax reference](/docs/reference/v3/filtering-query-syntax).

Search the links between product families and product attributes across your account. Each record is one family-attribute pair: `product_family_id`, `attribute_id`, `level`, and `account_id`.

> **Warning:** Always send a filter. This endpoint is not automatically scoped to your own account the way the rest of the v3 API is, so a call with no filter returns a result set that isn’t limited to your catalog. Filter by `account_id` to scope the search to your account, and add `product_family_id` to narrow it to a single family.

`level` is where the attribute sits in the family’s inheritance: `no_level`, `parent_level`, or `variant_level`. It can also come back `null` on links where it was never set. See [Data model](/docs/guides/data-model) for how family inheritance works.

To list one family’s attributes without the filtering caveat, use [Get-Family-Attributes Collection](/docs/reference/v3/familyattributes/get_family_attributes_collection_api_v3_product_families__product_family_id__attributes_get), which is scoped by its path.

Records carry attribute IDs, not full attribute definitions. Resolve names, types, and groups with [Search-Product-Attributes](/docs/reference/v3/productattributes/search_product_attributes_api_v3_product_attributes_get).

`_fields`, `_page`, and `_page_size` work as on the other search endpoints. See [Filtering and query syntax reference](/docs/reference/v3/filtering-query-syntax).

ChannelUpdateInputDto.title: ChannelUpdateInputDto
ChannelUpdateInputDto.description:
Input DTO for patching a channel.

``format`` is intentionally not patchable: it is the discriminator for which embedded
config (``shopify``/``wayfair``) and which top-level fields (``columns`` vs XML nodes)
actually apply, same reasoning as ``ConnectionUpdateInputDto`` excluding ``type``:
changing it mid-patch would desync the stored config from the format the rest of the
payload is being validated against.

Nullability follows the ``Channel`` entity field by field: fields declared ``X | None``
accept an explicit ``null``, fields declared bare (``name``, ``active``, list fields) do
not, since a ``None`` reaching ``Document.set()`` is not re-validated.

ChannelWebhookUpdateDto.title: ChannelWebhookUpdateDto

PATCH input for webhook config, reachable sub-field-by-sub-field via a sub-path PATCH.

``webhook_url`` is non-nullable because v1's ``WebhookSchema`` marks it ``required=True``.
The v1 resource merges this patch onto the channel's stored webhook before loading it, so
omitted siblings keep their current values.

``type`` is intentionally not patchable: the v1 manager selects the read/write schema
by the connection's *current* type, so changing it mid-patch would desync the
mongoengine discriminator from the schema used to validate the rest of the payload.

``token``/``refresh_token`` are intentionally not patchable: v1's marshmallow schema
doesn't declare them, so they'd be dropped from the loaded model while the raw payload
keys still reach ``ConnectionManager.patch``'s columns list, wiping the stored token
to ``None`` instead of leaving it untouched.

Nullability follows the concrete ``Connection`` subclasses: ``email`` lives only on
``DropboxConnection``, ``use_tls`` only on ``FtpConnection``. ``token_type``/``password``
exist only on the wire, with no entity field of that name.

PATCH input for eCatalog settings.

endpoint merges this patch onto the stored settings before load. The merge recurses, so

ECatalogUpdateInputDto.title: ECatalogUpdateInputDto
ECatalogUpdateInputDto.description:
Input DTO for patching an eCatalog.

List fields (``output_attributes``, ``notification_list``,
``quote_request_output_attributes``, ``exportable_attributes``) SET-replace with no
per-item merge on plytix-pim, so each item is sent complete and the CREATE item DTOs are
reused rather than kept as twins that could drift. ``settings`` is the one nested object
the PIM internal endpoint deep-merges onto the stored value, so it takes a dedicated
``Missing``-based UPDATE DTO whose sub-objects are patchable in turn.

Nullability follows v1's ``ECatalogSchema`` ``allow_none`` field by field, which is what
decides whether an explicit ``null`` survives to Mongo: fields v1 declares with
``allow_none=True`` accept ``null``, the rest do not. ``exportable_attributes`` is the one
place the two disagree — v1 permits ``null`` but ``ECatalog.exportable_attributes`` is a
non-nullable list, and a ``None`` reaching ``Document.set()`` is not re-validated, so the
stricter entity shape wins.

ProductAttributeUpdateInputDto.title: ProductAttributeUpdateInputDto
ProductAttributeUpdateInputDto.description:
Bound request superset for patching a product attribute.

Flat, not a discriminated union like create: ``type`` is not patchable, so there is no
discriminator in the PATCH body (nor in a reconstructed sub-path fragment) to resolve a
union at bind time. This DTO therefore accepts the union of every type's patchable field.

Per-type narrowing happens server-side: ``AttributeService.patch`` fetches the attribute's
concrete type and re-validates the set fields against the matching per-type subtype DTO
(see ``ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_TO_UPDATE_DTO``), rejecting fields that don't apply to that type.

``label``, ``group_ids`` and ``product_family_ids`` are intentionally not patchable:
v1's patch path doesn't handle ``label``/``groups``, and product-family attribute
membership is an async, destructive operation that must stay a separate job.

ProductFamilyUpdateInputDto.title: ProductFamilyUpdateInputDto
ProductFamilyUpdateInputDto.description:
Input DTO for patching a product family.

``name`` is the only patchable field. Attribute membership (``attributes``,
``parent_attributes``, ``variant_attributes``) is intentionally absent: in PIM those are
link/unlink/edit-level operations that return a Job, because the family write is followed
by an unbounded propagation across the family's products that also *deletes* attribute
values off variants whose parent now owns them. v1's own family PATCH reflects this by
hard-coding ``columns = ["name"]``, so an attribute field in the body would be silently
dropped; ``extra="forbid"`` rejects it instead.

v1 loads the family PATCH body without ``partial=True`` and its ``name`` is
``required=True``, so a patch that sets no field at all is rejected: the hook's own
empty-payload guard catches that before the PIM round-trip.

ProductUpdateInputDto.title: ProductUpdateInputDto
ProductUpdateInputDto.description:
Input DTO for patching a product.

All relation-id-list fields (``category_ids``, ``static_list_ids``, ``channel_ids``,
``ecatalog_ids``, ``product_data_sheet_ids``) are SET-replace: sending a list overwrites
the current one, ``[]`` clears it, omitting the field leaves it untouched.

``channel_ids``/``ecatalog_ids``/``product_data_sheet_ids`` require the account to have
UEF enabled — patching them otherwise is rejected (403), not silently ignored.

``gtin`` is non-nullable while its neighbour ``label`` is: PIM's ``ProductUpdateSchema``
declares ``gtin = fields.Str()`` with no ``allow_none``, so a forwarded ``null`` comes
back as ``{"gtin": ["Field may not be null."]}``. Rejecting it here turns that into a
field-level error at the kernel boundary instead of a PIM round-trip.
